slot.brief: Two gases at the same temperature (or the same gas at two temperatures); find the ratio of rms speeds using the v ∝ √(T/m) scaling, no absolute computation needed.

stem: At the same temperature, compare the rms speeds of molecules of hydrogen, H$_2$, and oxygen, O$_2$. What is the ratio $v_{\text{rms}}(\text{H}_2)/v_{\text{rms}}(\text{O}_2)$? Take their molar masses as $2$ g mol$^{-1}$ and $32$ g mol$^{-1}$, respectively.

verdicts.working: At the same temperature, rms speed is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass. The ratio is \(\sqrt{32/2}=4\).

working:
$v_{\text{rms}}\propto\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{M}}$ at fixed $T$.
$\dfrac{v_{\text{rms}}(\text{H}_2)}{v_{\text{rms}}(\text{O}_2)}=\sqrt{\dfrac{32}{2}}=4$

Independent check: At the same temperature, rms speed is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass. The ratio is \(\sqrt{32/2}=4\).
